## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Akitticariya* ("The Conduct of Akitti", Cp 1) is the opening text of the *Cariyāpiṭaka* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [Wood 2005]. It stands at the head of the collection's first section consisting of ten stories that illustrate the Bodhisatta's perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) [Wood 2005]. Unlike the canonical *Jātaka* collection, the *Cariyāpiṭaka* does not begin with an independent general introduction; instead, the first two verses of the *Akitticariya* simultaneously introduce the overall cycle of past-life stories and initiate this specific narrative [Wood 2005]. In these opening verses, the Buddha as narrator explains why he selected this birth story to commence the narrative of his former lives, acknowledging his countless births as a Bodhisatta over incalculable aeons [Wood 2005].
